summary: Proposes an Initial Connection Protocol, the opening handshake a user process such as Telnet uses to reach a server process such as a logger at another site. It describes a family of such protocols and picks one as the standard for connecting to systems with teletype-like terminals. It was replaced by RFC 165.

eli5.summary: The first time you call a friend, you need a standard way to start the call and move to a private line. This note proposes that opening routine for computers.

questions: what is the initial connection protocol
how does a user process connect to a logger
subtitle: A proposed opening handshake that lets a user process reach a server process, such as a Telnet login.

tldr.problem: A user process at one site needs a standard way to contact a server process at another site and end up with a connection pair in each direction.
tldr.mechanism: The user connects to a well-known send socket L, the server replies with a 32-bit even number S and closes, and then two new connections are made using sockets S and S+1.
tldr.outcome: The RFC proposes that one member of the family, with L equal to 1 and byte sizes of 8, become the official Telnet ICP. It was later obsoleted by RFC 165.

today: The metadata gives this RFC's status as unknown. It was obsoleted by RFC 165 and updated by RFC 127, RFC 143 and RFC 148.

sections.title: What an ICP Is
sections.content:
An Initial Connection Protocol (ICP) is a third level protocol started by a user process at one site to contact a server process at another. Typically the user process is a Telnet and the server is a logger, though other cases exist. The RFC describes a family of ICPs that set up one pair of connections, one in each direction, and proposes one member as the standard for hosts that accept teletype-like devices.

It obsoletes RFCs 66 and 80 and updates RFCs 98 and 101.
sections.eli5: An ICP is the polite way for one computer to knock on another's door and get set up to talk.

sections.title: Notation and Sockets
sections.content:
The author uses an ad hoc notation for system calls: Init tries to connect a local socket to a foreign socket with a byte size, Listen waits for a connection request, and Send, Receive and Close do what their names say.

A local socket number is 32 bits. A foreign socket number is 40 bits, whose high-order eight bits name the foreign Host. The byte size is an eight bit non-zero number. The sum of the local and foreign socket numbers must be odd.
sections.eli5: A socket is a numbered mailbox on a computer, and a connection joins one mailbox to another.

sections.title: The ICP Family
sections.content:
A server attaches a well-advertised send socket L and listens. The user connects from its receive socket U using byte size 32. The server sends a 32-bit even number S and closes. Sockets S and S+1 at the server are then connected to U+1 and U at the user, using byte sizes Bu and Bs.

An ICP is characterized by three numbers, L, Bs and Bu. L must be a send socket, Bs and Bu must be legal byte sizes, and each L has only one pair of byte sizes. That last rule stops two different services sharing one socket and being told apart only by byte size.
sections.eli5: The first call only tells you which private line to use. Then you hang up and use that line.

sections.title: The Proposed Telnet ICP
sections.content: For interactive, ASCII users connecting to hosts that serve them, the RFC proposes an ICP with L = 1 (specifically X00000001) and Bs = Bu = 8. The author asks that it be made official, with comments published before the May NWG meeting, where it would be accepted or rejected.
sections.eli5: For ordinary typing at a remote computer, the proposal picks one standard phone number and one standard way to talk.
